challenge.back_up: proceed, with the signal choice opened as a question for Akien
challenge.better_approach: Considered defaulting every sshd session to cc. It is the smallest change, but it misclasses Akien's own ssh, so it is one of the options put to him, not a default taken here.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That no physical signal exists today. Measured: same key (akien@akienasus, SHA256:rn8eUJ...), same source host 10.0.0.68, no CAIRN_USER/CLAUDECODE in the session environments, AcceptEnv only LANG LC_* COLORTERM NO_COLOR, and PermitUserEnvironment no.
challenge.prior_art: 8a53046951bb made CAIRN_USER and CLAUDECODE promote a caller to cc, and that environment does not cross ssh. b63f5bbbef89 walks the ancestry for tab scopes. Outline 17.2.1 settled the Windows process-chain reading. None of them covers an sshd session.
challenge.real_collision: Outline 17.2.1 says the only question is LLM or code. This ticket answers that question, it does not add an authoring-entity field. The approve gate in artifact.py relies on the akien class, and this ticket is what makes the gate true.

answers.falsifier: A caller under an sshd session that CC started classes cc, and approve refuses it. Akien's own ssh and local desktop scopes class as the answer to Q#115 rules. A journal entry written by akienasus's CC over ssh names class cc.
answers.from_idea: none, because this was measured, not imagined: caller() in cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py classes every logind session-*.scope as akien, and the live ssh sessions from akienasus (session-2609.scope, session-2620.scope, session-2667.scope) are CC's
answers.how: caller() in cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py reads a signal that separates CC-over-ssh from Akien-over-ssh. Which signal (a dedicated ssh key for CC, a forwarded LC_ variable, or something else) is Akien's to choose, as Q#115. Until it is chosen, BUILDME waits on the question. A red-first proof pins classify/caller over a scratch ancestry.
answers.traces_to: Law 7: the artifact journal is a record of truth, and it records CC's ssh writes as Akien's. Outline 17.2.1: the one writer question is LLM or code, and this answers it wrongly. Law 6: approve is Akien's gate, and today a CC ssh session passes it.
answers.what: A process that CC started over ssh classes as cc at the artifact door, so the journal, the question door and approve read an LLM's hand as an LLM's, never as Akien's.

bullets.text: Every write akienasus's CC makes on akiendelllinux over ssh is journaled as Akien's (1002 commons and 669 cairn journal entries), and approve, which admits only the akien class, would admit it. No approval has ever been journaled.
